records.text: Mamdani received 32% of the Jewish vote, according to a CNN exit poll of about 4,700 people.
records.speaker: Mark (Candace show producer; surname unverified)

appearances.snippet: 32% is pretty insane ... This is according to a CNN exit poll of about 4,700 people coming out.

verification.notes: CNN’s final exit-poll presentation reported Mamdani at 32% among Jewish voters, so the percentage is supported. CNN’s methodology report states that the New York City Voter Poll included 4,447 respondents, not about 4,700; the episode’s sample-size description overstates the total by 253 respondents. The underlying subgroup estimate also remains a poll estimate subject to sampling error.

records.text: Mark said the C-37A's call sign changed from REACH to SAM after departing Fort Huachuca, which told him the aircraft had picked up a senior official there
records.speaker: Mark (Candace show producer; surname unverified)

appearances.snippet: But once it gets to Fort Huachuca and takes off, it switches to SAM. So that tells me they picked up someone of that stature in Fort Huachuca.

verification.notes: AirNav Radar confirms that SAM702 on September 9, 2025 was U.S. Air Force C-37A registration 99-0404, Mode-S AE04F9, tracked in southern Arizona. The surviving public record does not establish an earlier RCH/REACH call sign, a call-sign change after departing Fort Huachuca, or the identity or seniority of any passenger. The SAM portion is supported; the claimed transition and passenger inference are not.

sources.title: Flight SAM702 — United States Air Force — AirNav Radar
sources.relevance: Confirms SAM702, registration 99-0404, Mode-S AE04F9, and southern-Arizona tracking on September 9, 2025, but not the claimed RCH-to-SAM transition or passenger.

records.text: CERN was established in 1954 to research particle physics.
records.speaker: Mark (Candace show producer; surname unverified)

appearances.snippet: And I just want to preface by saying I am not a particle physicist. So I'm just I just use particle physics recreationally. I'm a high school dropout. This is all on my own. But CERN was basically established in 1954 to research particle physics.

verification.notes: CERN's official history states that the organization began in 1954 and that fundamental physics has been its core business; CERN describes its main research area as particle physics.

sources.title: Our History — CERN
sources.relevance: Official CERN history confirms its 1954 establishment and fundamental/particle-physics research mission.

records.text: In 1964, a group of scientists including Peter Higgs theorized the Higgs boson.
records.speaker: Mark (Candace show producer; surname unverified)

appearances.snippet: And so in 1964, a group of scientists theorized that there's something called a Higgs boson, one of the scientists was named. and peter higgs i believe and so the search was on to find this particle

verification.notes: CERN states that Peter Higgs postulated the Higgs boson in 1964 alongside the independent work of Robert Brout and François Englert, matching the statement's description of a group of scientists including Higgs.

sources.title: CERN pays tribute to Peter Higgs
sources.relevance: Official CERN account confirms Higgs's 1964 postulate and the related work of Brout and Englert.

records.text: CERN's Large Hadron Collider is a 17-mile tunnel near Geneva, reaches roughly 600 feet underground in places, and collides subatomic particles at high speed.
records.speaker: Mark (Candace show producer; surname unverified)

appearances.snippet: and peter higgs i believe and so the search was on to find this particle and so that's why cern created the large hadron collider which is based in geneva switzerland and is a 17 mile tunnel underground up to 600 feet underground in some places where they shoot particles at subatomic particles at each other at a very high speed to try and break them apart to see what they're found what they're composed of

verification.notes: CERN describes the LHC as a 27-kilometre ring near Geneva where high-energy beams travel near light speed and collide. Its official guide gives tunnel depths of 50 to 175 metres, making the maximum about 574 feet and the statement's rough 600-foot figure reasonable.

sources.title: The Large Hadron Collider — CERN
sources.relevance: Official CERN page confirms the 27-km ring, Geneva-area location, high-speed beams, and collisions.

sources.title: LHC the guide — CERN
sources.relevance: Official CERN guide gives the tunnel depth range as 50 to 175 metres, approximately 574 feet at maximum.

records.text: In 2012, CERN observed a reaction consistent with the Higgs boson theorized in 1964.
records.speaker: Mark (Candace show producer; surname unverified)

appearances.snippet: and peter higgs i believe and so the search was on to find this particle and so that's why cern created the large hadron collider which is based in geneva switzerland and is a 17 mile tunnel underground up to 600 feet underground in some places where they shoot particles at subatomic particles at each other at a very high speed to try and break them apart to see what they're found what they're composed of and so in 2012 they observed a reaction reaction that's consistent with this particle that was theorized back in 1964 that they were calling some people were calling it the god particle

verification.notes: CERN states that ATLAS and CMS reached the five-sigma discovery threshold on 4 July 2012 and identified a new particle consistent with the long-sought Higgs boson proposed decades earlier. 'Observed a reaction' is imprecise, but the factual substance is correct.

sources.title: How did we discover the Higgs boson? — CERN
sources.relevance: Official CERN explanation confirms the 2012 discovery of a particle consistent with the Higgs boson.

records.text: Mamdani received 32% of the Jewish vote, according to a CNN exit poll.
records.speaker: Mark (Candace show producer; surname unverified)

appearances.snippet: 32% is pretty insane ... This is according to a CNN exit poll of about 4,700 people coming out.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous reports attribute the result to the CNN/SSRS exit poll, with publications reporting Mamdani’s Jewish-voter share as either 32% or 33%, apparently reflecting rounding or poll refreshes. The episode’s 32% figure is directly supported by Religion News Service, while JTA reported 33%. The substantive claim—about one-third—holds, but the exact percentage was not uniform across published versions.
